question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the RFC’s core Claw lifecycle, including package-declared files written into newly created agent workspaces under this consent and provenance model?
rationale: The patch creates durable core CLI, filesystem trust, persistence, and upgrade surfaces from an open RFC; implementation correctness cannot decide whether those product contracts should exist.

options.title: Pause pending RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep this protected stacked PR open but do not land it until maintainers accept or narrow the Claw lifecycle contract.

options.title: Sponsor the full stack
options.body: Approve the core direction and review the ordered add, package, status/remove, export, MCP, cron, and update slices as one lifecycle.

options.title: Narrow workspace ownership
options.body: Initially permit only canonical bootstrap files and defer arbitrary supporting workspace files until the broader lifecycle is accepted.

recommendation.title: Pause pending RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep this protected stacked PR open but do not land it until maintainers accept or narrow the Claw lifecycle contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to the shared state and fs-safe owner boundaries, making them the best routing candidate for the core product decision.
